summary: This diagram illustrates the architecture of a Transformer model, a key component in modern natural language processing. It features two main sections: the encoder and decoder, each containing multiple layers denoted as 'N×'. The encoder processes inputs through a series of 'Add & Norm' and 'Feed Forward' blocks, utilizing 'Multi-Head Attention' mechanisms. The decoder similarly employs 'Masked Multi-Head Attention' to ensure that predictions for a given position depend only on known outputs. The diagram also highlights the use of positional encoding to maintain the order of input sequences, culminating in output probabilities generated by a linear layer followed by a softmax function.
